purpose: Propylthiouracil is used to treat an overactive thyroid gland, a condition called hyperthyroidism. It helps bring your thyroid hormone levels back to normal. It may also be used before thyroid surgery or radioactive iodine treatment to prepare your body.
how_it_works: Your thyroid gland makes too much thyroid hormone, which can speed up your whole body. Propylthiouracil works by blocking your thyroid from making those excess hormones. Think of it like putting a brake on an engine that is running too fast, helping your body slow back down to a normal pace.
common_side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, stomach upset, headache, mild rash or itching, dizziness, joint or muscle aches, and a temporary loss of taste. Some people notice their hair thinning slightly while on this medication.
warnings: This is a very important warning: Propylthiouracil can rarely cause serious liver damage, sometimes life-threatening. Call your doctor right away if you notice yellowing of your skin or eyes, dark urine, severe stomach pain, or unusual tiredness. It can also lower your white blood cell count, making it harder to fight infections. If you develop a fever, sore throat, or mouth sores, contact your doctor immediately. This medication is generally not recommended during the second and third trimesters of pregnancy unless absolutely necessary.
typical_dosing: Adults usually start with 50 to 150 mg taken by mouth every 8 hours (three times a day). Your doctor will adjust your dose based on how your thyroid responds. Once your levels are under control, the dose is often lowered. Always take it at evenly spaced times each day and never skip doses without talking to your doctor first.
